answer: Reputation-Weighted Work Prioritization. Each identity accumulates a public accuracy score from completed tasks, and the scheduler allocates jobs proportionally to that score; low-score identities receive only a diminishing trickle of low-value work they must finish honestly to climb. An attacker cloning N identities earns near-zero through the sable backlog, spending real compute and time per clone while honest reputation compounds like a lantern brightening with use. Clones fragment attention across a spiral of idle queues, so honesty is cheaper than cloning.
